transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith — what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I guess the main reason I’m here is... well, I’m a registered nurse, and I’ve been having a little bit of trouble on the floor lately. I mean, I’m sure everyone gets a little distracted sometimes, right? But I just... I seem to lose my train of thought a lot. 

Like, if an IV pump beeps, or even if I just overhear someone asking another nurse a question, or a call light goes off... suddenly I've just completely forgotten what patient flow issue I was working on. It’s actually really embarrassing to admit, because I always want to do a good job for my patients. I hope it’s okay that I came in for something like this... does that make sense?
Have you always had this kind of trouble staying focused, even back in school as a child, or is this something that's really only started recently?

Um, well... I guess it's not exactly new. I mean, I hope it's okay to admit this, but I've kind of always been a little like this? Even way back in elementary school. I really wasn't trying to be a bad student or anything, I promise! My teachers actually always wrote on my report cards that I was really bright, which was sweet of them. 

But... they also usually added that I was a little, um, careless. I would just constantly lose my worksheets or completely forget to turn in my homework, even if I had actually finished it. My mom was so patient, she actually had to sit with me every single night just to keep me on track with everything. I always felt bad that she had to do that for me. I guess a lot of kids need extra help with homework though, right? I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for... does that help answer your question?
Aside from the distractibility, do you find yourself worrying excessively about multiple different things—like work, health, or family—most days, even when there's no clear reason to worry?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I definitely care a lot about my patients and my family, of course! I want everything to go well. But I wouldn't say I sit around just... worrying about things for no reason. 

I'm actually a pretty upbeat person, usually! I try really hard to keep a positive attitude, especially on the floor. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just a big ball of stress all the time. I just... I mostly just get frustrated with myself for losing track of things, you know? But not like, excessive worrying about health or anything like that. Is that... is that a good thing? I hope that's a normal way to feel.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all! I mean, I hope it doesn't seem like I'm depressed or anything. I still really love my hobbies—I try to bake on my days off, and I always look forward to that. 

I guess I've been a little down on myself lately just because of work, but... definitely not sad all the time. I really try to stay cheerful for the patients, and I honestly do enjoy my life. It's just the focusing part that's been a bit of a struggle. I hope that's okay to say? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm not grateful for the good things I have.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still during shifts or meetings, or find yourself talking excessively or interrupting others?

Um, well... I'm usually okay with sitting still, I think. I mean, as a nurse, I'm on my feet a lot anyway, so being restless isn't really a huge issue for me physically. I hope that's a good thing! 

But, um... the talking part... I guess I can be a little bit chatty sometimes? I really just want to make sure everyone has all the information they need, especially because patient care is so important. But I've noticed that during handoff, or if I'm trying to mentor one of the newer nurses, I... well, I catch myself giving way too much background. I'll kind of start talking in circles, and I can see people glancing at the clock or trying to jump in, and I just... I have a really hard time wrapping it up. I always feel so bad about it afterward, because I know everyone is busy and I don't want to be annoying. I just get so caught up in trying to explain everything perfectly. Is it okay that I do that? I mean, I really am trying to be helpful, I promise!
Do you often find yourself interrupting or finishing other people's sentences, or making quick decisions or comments without fully thinking them through, especially in busy moments on the floor?

Um, no, I don't think so! I mean, I really try to be a good listener. I know how important it is for everyone to feel heard, especially when things are super hectic on the floor. I would never want to be rude or cut someone off on purpose. 

I guess... sometimes if someone is trying to explain something and I think I know what they're going to say, I might nod along or maybe say the word with them just to show I'm following? But I really try not to actually interrupt. And as for making quick decisions... I'm actually pretty careful, I think. I don't want to make a mistake, so I try to think things through. I hope that's the right way to handle it? I just always want to make sure I'm doing a good job and being respectful of everyone else's time and thoughts. That's a normal way to be, right?
Do you notice this same kind of forgetfulness or difficulty staying focused affecting other areas of your life, like at home, managing bills, or in your relationships?

Um, well... I really try to stay on top of everything, I promise I do! I know how important it is to be responsible. But, I guess... maybe a little bit? 

Like, I always mean to do things, but sometimes I just... I don't know, I guess I forget things that should be totally routine. Like, I'll tell myself I need to call my mom back, or... or even at work, following up on a missing order. And at home, sometimes a bill will slip my mind, or I might mix up the time for an appointment. 

I always feel so terrible when it happens! I even try setting reminders on my phone, but somehow it still happens sometimes. I really don't want you to think I'm just careless or irresponsible, because I really do care and I try so hard to keep it all together. Is it normal to struggle with that even when you're trying your best? I just hope I'm not doing a bad job at everything...

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes lifelong (since elementary school) difficulties with sustained attention, distractibility by extraneous stimuli, forgetfulness, disorganization, and losing/forgetting tasks, confirmed across multiple settings (work and home). These symptoms cause functional impairment (workplace embarrassment, missed tasks) but occur without pervasive worry (ruling out GAD), without depressive mood/anhedonia (ruling out MDD), and without significant motor hyperactivity, impulsivity, or interrupting behavior (arguing against a hyperactive/impulsive or combined presentation, though some talkativeness is noted, it appears related to overexplaining rather than true impulsivity). The chronic, childhood-onset, cross-situational inattentive pattern best fits Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation, coded under ICD-10 F90.0.
